g.data-info: The thin outer wall of the grain; in maize the fruit wall and seed coat are fused together.
Large starchy food store that nourishes the embryo during germination.
Single protein-rich outer layer of the endosperm that releases enzymes to digest stored food during germination.
The single shield-shaped cotyledon that absorbs food from the endosperm for the embryo.
Protective sheath enclosing the plumule as it grows up through the soil.
The embryonic shoot with young leaves, enclosed by the coleoptile.
Short axis joining plumule and radicle where the scutellum is attached.
Protective sheath that covers the radicle until it emerges.
The embryonic root, enclosed by the coleorhiza.
